messages.author: Tristan Manfred Stöber
messages.title: [Jobs] 2 PhD + 1 Postdoc + 2 RA positions: hippocampus, world models, epilepsy (Göttingen)
messages.body_html: Dear all, I am looking for five people to join my group at the Campus Institute Data Science (CIDAS), University of Göttingen, Germany. We study how the brain builds and uses its internal model of the world, and how those principles can be reengineered in artificial neural networks. In parallel, we run a clinical line of work on epilepsy, applying machine learning tools to intracranial recordings from patients, together with the University Hospital Frankfurt. All positions are based in Göttingen and start as soon as possible. PH.D. STUDENT - HIPPOCAMPAL REPRESENTATIONS IN DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENTS TV-L E13 100%, 3 years Analyse an unpublished, large-scale in-vivo miniscope dataset: CA1 pyramidal cells tracked across 11 tasks and 34 days. Characterise how cognitive maps emerge, drift and are reused, from single cells to the geometry of the population manifold. In close collaboration with Tom McHugh (RIKEN CBS, Japan). PH.D. STUDENT - BRAIN-INSPIRED WORLD MODELS FOR DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENTS TV-L E13 100%, 3 years We distil inductive biases from normative hippocampus models and use these insights to build novel and powerful model-based deep RL agents. The goal: agents that plan over long horizons with interpretable internal representations. POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER - MACHINE LEARNING FOR EPILEPSY TV-L E13 100%, ~1 year with potential extension We try to predict epilepsy before it even starts. We use unique intracranial recordings from patients who suffered a bleed on the brain's surface, about one in three of whom go on to develop epilepsy. On these data we fine-tune EEG foundation models. We also build digital twin network models of individual patients, allowing us to simulate personalised prevention and treatment strategies. A collaboration with Michael Strüber and Felix Rosenow (University Hospital Frankfurt), and Richard Gao (Goethe University Frankfurt). RESEARCH ASSISTANTS (2 POSITIONS) Part-time, students welcome Support the projects above with calcium imaging data processing, behavioural tracking, software engineering and simulation experiments. A good entry point for a B.Sc. or M.Sc. thesis in the lab. PREREQUISITES Strong quantitative skills, fluency in Python, experience with machine learning, and genuine curiosity about both brains and machines. WHAT WE OFFER An interdisciplinary group at the interface of neuroscience and AI, a strong national and international network, and a generous ERC travel and publication budget for conferences such as NeurIPS, Cosyne and FENS. HOW TO APPLY Send your CV, a short motivation letter naming the position you are interested in, and contact details of two references to EMAIL_REDACTED. Applications received by 24 September 2026 will receive full consideration; the positions remain open until filled. Internships and thesis projects outside these openings are always welcome. If you are unsure which position fits you best, or would like to hear more about a project before applying, write to me at the same address. I am happy to talk first. More about the lab at [1]. Best regards, Tristan [1] https://tristanstoeber.github.io Tristan Manfred Stöber, Ph.D. Computational Neuroscientist CIDAS Fellow, Campus Institute Data Science, University of Göttingen Research Fellow, Dept. of Neurology, University Hospital Frankfurt

Dear all,

I am looking for five people to join my group at the Campus Institute
Data Science (CIDAS), University of Göttingen, Germany. We study how
the brain builds and uses its internal model of the world, and how
those principles can be reengineered in artificial neural networks.
In parallel, we run a clinical line of work on epilepsy, applying
machine learning tools to intracranial recordings from patients,
together with the University Hospital Frankfurt.

All positions are based in Göttingen and start as soon as possible.

PH.D. STUDENT - HIPPOCAMPAL REPRESENTATIONS IN DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENTS
TV-L E13 100%, 3 years
Analyse an unpublished, large-scale in-vivo miniscope dataset: CA1
pyramidal cells tracked across 11 tasks and 34 days. Characterise how
cognitive maps emerge, drift and are reused, from single cells to the
geometry of the population manifold. In close collaboration with Tom
McHugh (RIKEN CBS, Japan).

PH.D. STUDENT - BRAIN-INSPIRED WORLD MODELS FOR DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENTS
TV-L E13 100%, 3 years
We distil inductive biases from normative hippocampus models and use
these insights to build novel and powerful model-based deep RL agents.
The goal: agents that plan over long horizons with interpretable
internal representations.

POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER - MACHINE LEARNING FOR EPILEPSY
TV-L E13 100%, ~1 year with potential extension
We try to predict epilepsy before it even starts. We use unique
intracranial recordings from patients who suffered a bleed on the
brain's surface, about one in three of whom go on to develop epilepsy.
On these data we fine-tune EEG foundation models. We also build digital
twin network models of individual patients, allowing us to simulate
personalised prevention and treatment strategies. A collaboration with
Michael Strüber and Felix Rosenow (University Hospital Frankfurt), and
Richard Gao (Goethe University Frankfurt).

RESEARCH ASSISTANTS (2 POSITIONS)
Part-time, students welcome
Support the projects above with calcium imaging data processing,
behavioural tracking, software engineering and simulation experiments.
A good entry point for a B.Sc. or M.Sc. thesis in the lab.

PREREQUISITES
Strong quantitative skills, fluency in Python, experience with machine
learning, and genuine curiosity about both brains and machines.

WHAT WE OFFER
An interdisciplinary group at the interface of neuroscience and AI, a
strong national and international network, and a generous ERC travel
and publication budget for conferences such as NeurIPS, Cosyne and
FENS.

HOW TO APPLY
Send your CV, a short motivation letter naming the position you are
interested in, and contact details of two references to
EMAIL_REDACTED.

Applications received by 24 September 2026 will receive full
consideration; the positions remain open until filled. Internships and
thesis projects outside these openings are always welcome.

If you are unsure which position fits you best, or would like to hear
more about a project before applying, write to me at the same address.
I am happy to talk first.

More about the lab at [1].

Best regards,
Tristan

topics.title: 2 postdoc and 1 phD positions on computational mechanisms of human perception (Alex Hyafil & Chris Summerfield, Barcelona)
topics.snippet: The group of Alex Hyafil at the CRM Barcelona (https://ahyafil.github.io/) is looking for two postdoc

messages.author: Alexandre Hyafil
messages.title: 2 postdoc and 1 phD positions on computational mechanisms of human perception (Alex Hyafil & Chris Summerfield, Barcelona)
messages.body_html:
The group of Alex Hyafil at the CRM Barcelona (https://ahyafil.github.io/) is looking for two postdoc researchers and a PhD student.  

One of the postdoc positions will be co-supervised by Chris Summerfield (Universitat Pompeu Fabra Barcelona / Oxford; https://humaninformationprocessing.com/). The selected candidate will investigate the computational operations underlying visual scene perception through a combination of simulation of artificial visual systems (conv nets, visual transformers) and human experiments. The position is for two years.

The other postdoc researcher (2-year duration) and the PhD student (4-year) will work jointly on identifying canonical Bayesian operations at play in human visual and auditory perception. The project involves Bayesian modelling, artificial vision network simulations, behavioral and EEG experiments as well as intra-cranial EEG experiments (in collaboration with Benjamin Morillon, AMU Marseille). We will look for complementarity of the two profiles, notably in terms of quantitative and experimental backgrounds.  

 

The hired researchers will benefit from the stimulating environment of the Barcelona area in cognitive and computational neuroscience. Our groups form part of a larger interacting network of neuroscience labs in Barcelona (http://www.barccsyn.org). Financial support is provided by the Spanish National Agency of Investigation (FPI fellowship for the PhD student).

 

APPLICATION: Send a curriculum and motivation letter with a list of two contacts for recommendation letter at https://bit.ly/ChrisAlexPositions. Informal enquiries are welcome.

DEADLINE: before October 31 for the PhD position; until position is filled for the postdoc positions.

STARTING DATE: before July 2027 for the PhD position; flexible for the postdoc positions

messages.author: Michael Graupner
messages.title: NeuralNet 2026, Nov 25th-27th, Paris – Registration and Abstract Submission Now Open
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues, 

We are pleased to announce the opening of registrations for NeuralNet 2026 Paris (Nov. 25th-27th, Odéon Campus of Université Paris Cité, 75006 Paris, France)

The program will explore four broad themes — Neural Codes & Representations, Perception in Context, Learning, Memory & Adaptation, and Brain States & Network Dynamics — bringing together leading researchers working across systems and computational neuroscience. We also encourage the submission of contributed talks and posters. 

Participants are invited to join the famous spike sorting mini-school before the conference (23-25 November). The mini-school is free of charge but registration is required.

👉 More information & registration 👈

We look forward to receiving your contributions and to welcoming you to Paris in November for three days of exciting science, discussion, and networking with the Systems and Computational Neuroscience community.

Best regards,

The NeuralNet 2026 Organizing Committee


--

topics.title: COSYNE 2027: Meeting announcement, Abstract submission is now open

messages.author: Tomas Hromadka
messages.title: COSYNE 2027: Meeting announcement, Abstract submission is now open
messages.body_html:
====================================================

Computational and Systems Neuroscience 2027 (Cosyne)

MAIN MEETING & WORKSHOPS
11 - 16 March 2027
Montreal, Canada

www.cosyne.org

====================================================


----------------------------------------------------
MEETING ANNOUNCEMENT
----------------------------------------------------

The annual Cosyne meeting provides an inclusive forum for the exchange of empirical and theoretical approaches to problems in systems neuroscience, in order to understand how neural systems function.

The MAIN MEETING is single-track. A set of invited talks is selected by the Executive Committee, and additional talks and posters are selected by the Program Committee, based on submitted abstracts. The WORKSHOPS feature in-depth discussion of current topics of interest, in a small group setting.

All abstract submissions will be reviewed double blind. The deadline for Abstract submission is 18 October 2026.

Cosyne topics include but are not limited to: neural basis of behavior, sensory and motor systems, circuitry, learning, neural coding, natural scene statistics, dendritic computation, neural basis of persistent activity, nonlinear receptive field mapping, representations of time and sequence, reward systems, decision-making, synaptic plasticity, map formation and plasticity, population coding, attention, neuromodulation, and computation with spiking networks.

We would like to foster increased participation from experimental groups as well as computational ones. Please circulate widely and encourage your students and postdocs to apply.


IMPORTANT DATES

Abstract submission is now open.
Abstract submission deadline: 18 October 2026


When preparing an abstract, authors should be aware that not all abstracts can be accepted for the meeting. Abstracts will be selected based on the clarity with which they convey the substance, significance, and originality of the work to be presented.


COSYNE INVITED SPEAKERS
Dani Bassett (UPenn)
Chand Chandrasekaran (Boston U)
Christine Constantinople (NYU)
Paul Cisek (U Montreal)
Kevin Franks (Duke)
Leslie P Kaelbling (MIT)
Andy Leifer (Princeton)
Scott Linderman (Stanford)
Amy Orsborne (U Washington)
Cengiz Pehlevan Kempner (Harvard)
Kanaka Rajan (Harvard; Kempner Inst)
Rebecca Saxe (MIT)
Carsen Stringer (Janelia)


ORGANIZING COMMITTEE
General Chairs: Kimberly Stachenfeld (DeepMind) and Mark Histed (NIH)
Program Chairs: Annegret Falkner (Princeton) and Guillaume Lajoie (MILA/U Montreal)
Workshop Chairs: N Alex Cayco Gajic (ENS) and Marcelo Mattar (NYU)
Tutorial Chairs: Eva Dyer (Georgia Tech) and Alex Williams (NYU)
Mentorship and Networking Chairs: Renata Brito (Mount Sinai) and Srikanth Ramaswamy (Newcastle U)
Undergraduate Travel Chairs: Lea Duncker (Columbia) and Kevin Miller (DeepMind)
Development Chair: Michael Long (NYU)
Media Chairs: Roxana Zeraati (MPI Biol Cybernetics) and Claire Sturgill (TU Dresden)
Poster Design: Maja Bialon


EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE
Stephanie Palmer (U Chicago)
Anne-Marie Oswald (U Pittsburgh)
Alexandre Pouget (U Geneva)
Anthony Zador (CSHL)


CONTACT
meeting [at] cosyne.org


-----------------------------------------------------
COSYNE MAILING LISTS
-----------------------------------------------------

Please consider adding yourself to Cosyne mailing lists (groups) to receive email updates with various Cosyne-related information and join in helpful discussions. See Cosyne.org -> About-> Mailing lists for details.

messages.body_html:
Dear all,

The registration for the EEG/EMG Foundation Challenge 2026 is now open: 

Last year, the EEG Foundation Challenge 2025 brought together 1,197 teams, 247 institutions, 50+ countries & 8,622 submissions. This year it returns with a broader scope and a few surprises! 

Four competition tracks across EEG & EMG, new dataset releases, and $20,000 in awards. 
One common goal: build biosignal decoding models that generalize beyond the conditions they were trained on. 

📅 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 
Sep 21: Submissions open 
Sep 21 → Oct 25: Warm-up phase (develop, test & iterate with feedback) 
Oct 25 → Nov 21: Final phase (evaluation on hidden data) 
Dec 11 & 12: Winners' ceremony at the NeurIPS Brain & Body Workshop, Sydney 

🏆 $𝟮𝟬,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗼𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗮𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱𝘀, funded by Meta, Muse® by Interaxon Inc. & Yneuro. 4 tracks, 3 winning teams per track, plus a prize for the best all-round performance and extra opportunities including internships & publications! Get a head start: public datasets, starter kit & baselines are live now through NeuralBench. Pick one track or all four and dive in! 

𝗕𝗲𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗲𝘁𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. Led by Bruno Aristimunha. Hosted by Yneuro & Inria, with Arnault Caillet & Sylvain Chevallier on coordination and platform, alongside Pierre Guetschel, Thomas Moreau, Lionel Kusch, Seyed Shirazi, Thomas Semah & Arnaud Delorme.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸𝘀, 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗷𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗯𝘆 𝗮𝗰𝗮𝗱𝗲𝗺𝗶𝗮 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘆
01 · EEG-to-Image (register)| AI at Meta FAIR Brain & AI (Hubert Banville, Jean-Rémi King, Joséphine Raugel) · Alljoined (Vinay Jayaram)
02 · BCI Decoding (register)| Inria (Simon Kojima, Pauline Dreyer, Raphaëlle Nina Roy, Fabien Lotte, Thorir Mar Ingolfsson, Marie-Constance Corsi)
03 · Sleep Onset (register)| Muse (Jiansheng Niu, Maurice Abou Jaoude, Chris Aimone)
04 · EMG-to-Pose (register)| Meta Reality Labs (Alexandre Gramfort, Cédric Rommel, Richard Warren, Tiberiu Tesileanu) · Imperial College London (Pranav Mamidanna, Arnault Caillet) 

Senior advisors: Scott Makeig, Terry Sejnowski, and Isabelle Guyon. 

See you on the leaderboard!

messages.body_html:
Hello,

My name is Andrea Bedorin, Communications and Project Officer at EBRAINS.

Since I think it might be interesting for the community, I would like to share the information on the EBRAINS Users Days 2026, taking place in Heidelberg on 6-7 October. 

Who should attend?

The event is relevant to researchers and professionals working across neuroscience, neurology, brain health and related fields who would like to discover how EBRAINS tools and services can support their work.

What is it about?

The EBRAINS Users Days 2026 are designed for both newcomers and experienced users of the EBRAINS Research Infrastructure.

On 6 October, introductory presentations will show participants how EBRAINS can support their research. On 7 October, hands-on tutorials will offer practical experience with a broad range of EBRAINS tools and services.

Programme and registration:

https://flagship.kip.uni-heidelberg.de/jss/HBPm?m=SgD&mI=289&showAbstract=-1

Registration fee: €25 per day, including lunch at the Heidelberg University canteen, coffee breaks and refreshments.

Contact

Should you have any questions please contact: EMAIL_REDACTED

Join us a the EINC Heidelberg, Heidelberg, Germany!

Thank you very much for your consideration and support.

Best regards,

Andrea Bedorin

topics.snippet: Why are brains the way they are? Do neural circuits function in an “optimal” way, and if so, in what

messages.author: Andrew Lin
messages.title: Postdoctoral positions in sensory coding and memory - University of Sheffield
messages.body_html:
Why are brains the way they are? Do neural circuits function in an “optimal” way, and if so, in what sense are they optimal? How does the brain encode sensory information and form associative memories? Andrew Lin’s lab at the University of Sheffield is seeking up to two Research Associates to study these questions in the fruit fly Drosophila.

We study memory using a range of methods, such as in vivo two-photon calcium imaging, electrophysiology, fly genetics, behavioural experiments, computational modelling and building custom equipment. You will design, develop and perform experiments and data analysis (tailoring the project to your own interests and expertise), write papers, and present your work at conferences and seminars.

We seek self-motivated, innovative and creative candidates with a PhD (or be close to completion / have equivalent postdoctoral level experience) in a relevant field, expertise in at least some of the above techniques, excellent communication skills, and an ability to work independently and in a team. We encourage applications from diverse academic backgrounds, such as biology, neuroscience, experimental psychology, computer science, physics and engineering. 

Closing date: 5 October 2026
Apply at this link: https://tinyurl.com/LinPostdoc2026 or https://jobsite.sheffield.ac.uk/job/Research-Associate-Neuroscience-%282-Posts%29/3131-en_GB
More about the lab: https://www.aclinlab.org/
Start date is flexible - happy to discuss
We welcome international applicants and the university will reimburse the post-holder for many visa expenses: https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/jobs/induction/before/international/visas
For informal enquiries, contact Andrew: EMAIL_REDACTED


--

messages.title: PhD or Postdoctoral Position in Honey Bee Visual Navigation
messages.body_html:
We are recruiting a scientist to join us in the Straw Lab at the University of Freiburg, Germany.

The scientist will work on the neural and computational mechanisms of visual navigation in honey bees.

Read more about the position and submit applications at https://uni-freiburg.de/en/job/00005148/

I’d be happy to discuss the position or answer questions.

I’d also be grateful if you could forward this announcement to potentially interested people or networks.
